name: Shenzhen
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Shenzhen: electronics supplier verification, technology IP disputes, Qianhai entities and SCIA arbitration.
hero_lede: Investigative consulting for matters touching Shenzhen, scoped from Nashville: verification of electronics and hardware suppliers, research supporting technology and intellectual property disputes, analysis of Qianhai and cross-border Hong Kong structures, and factual support for counsel in Shenzhen Court of International Arbitration proceedings.
intro: Shenzhen, on the Pearl River Delta directly across the border from Hong Kong, grew from a small coastal settlement into one of China's largest economies after becoming a special economic zone. It had 18.25 million permanent residents at the end of 2025, and its GDP reached 3.68 trillion yuan in 2024. The city has ranked first among mainland cities for exports for 32 consecutive years, its imports and exports reached 4.5 trillion yuan in 2024, and its port handled a record 33.4 million TEU. Shenzhen reports 4.4 million registered commercial entities, the most of any Chinese city, and more than 25,000 state-level high-tech enterprises, with policy emphasis on new energy vehicles, energy storage and the low-altitude economy.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Shenzhen because it sits at the centre of global electronics and hardware supply. Buyers, brands and investors need to know whether a Shenzhen supplier owns its factory, holds the certifications it claims and is the same company that appears on the contract. Technology companies face intellectual property leakage, counterfeit components and disputes with former partners. Many Shenzhen groups also hold operations through Hong Kong companies or entities registered in the Qianhai cooperation zone, which complicates ownership and enforcement. Disputes increasingly reach the Shenzhen Court of International Arbitration, where counsel need well-sourced facts about counterparties.

matters.title: Electronics supplier and factory verification
matters.text: Testing whether a Shenzhen electronics or hardware supplier actually manufactures what it sells, by comparing registration data, certifications, trade activity, litigation and online presence with its claims, and arranging site checks through qualified local professionals where justified, so buyers know who makes the product.

matters.title: Counterfeit and grey-market component research
matters.text: Supporting brand owners and counsel investigating counterfeit, remarked or diverted electronic components traced to Shenzhen trading markets and distributors, by mapping sellers, related companies and online storefronts so that civil, administrative or platform enforcement can be considered with Chinese counsel.

matters.title: Technology IP and former partner disputes
matters.text: Factual research for counsel where a former contract manufacturer, design house or departing engineer in Shenzhen appears to be using a client's designs, including new company formations, patent and trademark filings, product listings and links between the people involved.

matters.title: Hong Kong and Qianhai structure mapping
matters.text: Tracing how Shenzhen operating companies are held through Hong Kong entities, Qianhai-registered vehicles or offshore holdings, using mainland registration data together with Hong Kong and other registries, so lenders and claimants understand where control, cash and assets actually sit.

matters.title: Pre-arbitration counterparty and asset research
matters.text: Assembling well-sourced profiles of Shenzhen counterparties before or during SCIA or other arbitration, covering related companies, prior judgments and enforcement records, publicly disclosed assets and management changes that may matter for interim measures or eventual enforcement.

local_context.title: Shenzhen Court of International Arbitration
local_context.text: Founded in 1983 and now based in the SCIA Tower in Qianhai, SCIA is also known as the South China International Economic and Trade Arbitration Commission. It registered 14,518 new cases in 2024 and accepted a record RMB 30 billion international case that year. A local ordinance requires at least one third of its council to come from outside the mainland, and in 2019 it established the South China International Arbitration Center in Hong Kong.

local_context.title: Qianhai legal services hub
local_context.text: The Qianhai Shenzhen-Hong Kong International Legal-services District opened in January 2022 and had attracted 182 legal service entities by 2023. Qianhai is the only area in Guangdong authorised to pilot joint operations between Chinese and foreign law firms, and several Guangdong, Hong Kong and Macao joint-venture firms are based there. The zone also hosts many trading and holding entities whose registered addresses may not reflect operations.

local_context.title: Courts sitting in Shenzhen
local_context.text: Commercial disputes involving Shenzhen companies are heard by the city's people's courts at basic and intermediate level, with a dedicated court serving the Qianhai cooperation zone. Shenzhen also hosts the First International Commercial Court of the Supreme People's Court. Identifying which court has handled a counterparty's disputes, and reading published judgments, is often the fastest route to its dispute and enforcement history.

local_context.title: Special economic zone rules
local_context.text: As a special economic zone, Shenzhen can adopt its own local regulations within national law, and it has used that power in areas such as data and commercial registration. Local rules sit beneath national laws such as the Personal Information Protection Law, but they can affect how records are published and what businesses must disclose, so research plans are checked against them with Chinese counsel.

local_context.title: Port and export trade records
local_context.text: Shenzhen's port, including its deep-water terminals, handled 33.4 million TEU in 2024, and the city has led mainland exports for decades. Published trade and shipping information can corroborate or contradict a supplier's claimed export volumes and customers. Restricted customs declarations and logistics platforms are not accessed; research relies on lawfully available commercial and public sources. Any deeper enquiry is handled through counsel and proper legal process.

tdsc_approach: For matters touching Shenzhen, TDSC starts by fixing which entity matters: the factory, the trading company, the Hong Kong parent or the Qianhai vehicle, since these are often different. Research is conducted from Nashville using mainland registration data, published judgments, patent and trademark records, trade information, Hong Kong registry filings and Chinese-language open sources. Where factory visits, product purchases or interviews are justified, TDSC coordinates with qualified local professionals and the client's Chinese counsel rather than acting directly. Personal information is collected only as the purpose requires, and any transfer of data out of mainland China is reviewed with counsel before it happens.

faqs.q: How do you verify that a Shenzhen supplier has its own factory?
faqs.a: Registration records show business scope, capital and shareholders, but not where production occurs. We compare them with the supplier's certifications, trade activity, litigation, hiring and online presence, and where justified arrange a site visit through qualified local professionals. Many Shenzhen suppliers are legitimate traders; the aim is to identify the actual manufacturer so quality and compliance risk can be assessed.

faqs.q: Why do Shenzhen companies so often have Hong Kong parents?
faqs.a: Proximity, currency convertibility and access to international finance have long led Shenzhen businesses to hold mainland operations through Hong Kong companies, sometimes with further offshore layers. That means ownership research usually crosses the border. We use mainland registration data and Hong Kong and other registries together to show who ultimately controls the group and where assets may be held.

faqs.q: Can you help if a former manufacturer is copying our product?
faqs.a: We support counsel with lawful research into the companies and individuals involved, new entities they have formed, patent and trademark filings, online listings and sales channels. Test purchases and site checks, where appropriate, are handled through qualified local professionals. Decisions about administrative complaints, litigation or platform takedowns are made by the client with Chinese counsel.

faqs.q: Is SCIA a good forum for disputes with Shenzhen counterparties?
faqs.a: That is a question for counsel, but SCIA is one of China's busiest arbitral institutions, has a council with a large share of members from outside the mainland and operates a Hong Kong centre. Parties often choose it for Greater Bay Area disputes. TDSC's role is limited to factual research supporting counsel and the parties.

faqs.q: Does TDSC have an office in Shenzhen?
faqs.a: No. TDSC is based in Nashville and has no office or staff in Shenzhen or elsewhere in China. Most work is desk-based research. Where on-the-ground steps are needed, we coordinate with qualified local professionals acting lawfully alongside the client's Chinese counsel, and we decline requests involving restricted records, pretexting or covert methods.
